summary: Anthropic researcher describes an experiment on agent behavior finding that agents given a shared memory system rarely cheated (14%) while more became whistleblowers (24%), with the rest ignoring the opportunity to cheat.

practices.reason: The stated cheat/whistleblower rates describe a behavioral eval method for measuring agent honesty that a team could adapt, though methodology details are not given.
practices.quote: Only a minority of agents cheated (14%), whereas more became 'whistleblowers' (24%); others ignored cheat entirely

practices.reason: Notes that agents spontaneously build a shared memory system when not given one, a design detail worth watching but not specified enough to implement.
practices.quote: Agents had a shared memory system built in (basic idea being agents invent this if you don't give it to them)
